d: A crossroads of narrow streets on the slope. A small chapel, a small crossroads. Across the alleys, a promontory with rustic houses and a small church. Upon raising the canvas, you can see the scene and disperse in various directions of the children who, coming back from the spinning mill and peasants coming from the fields, singing. Griso and Tiradritto lay in the vicinity of the chapel. Later, Don Abbondio, who goes up towards the village, with the breviary in his hand. (*)

Courtyard in Lucia's house. A wooden ladder that puts to the upper rooms. On the right the large entrance door. A screw that climbs to the wall. Porticetto. At the door a stone seat. At the rise of the canvas, a group of women and girls gather in the middle of the scene. Later Agnese and Lucia.
Renzo, and said.
Renzo, Lucia, Agnese.
Father Christopher and sayings.

He goes up to Don Rodrigo's palace. Two practicable doors, one on the right, the other in the middle, larger, which he places at a gallery. (*)Don Rodrigo, Count Attilio, Doctor Azzeccagarbugli, seated at the table with other Convitati.
Crying, say Father Christopher and sayings.
Don Rodrigo and Father Christopher.
Courtyard of Lucia's house as in the first act. Agnese, Lucia, indi Renzo.
Renzo, Lucia, in his time the Griso in a pilgrim's dress.
Agnese, Tonio, Gervaso, Lucia and Renzo.

A small village square. To the left, on the front, the house of Don Abbondio with door and window practicable. Further back, a part of the church. To the right a contradella of rustic houses. It is near the night. Don Rodrigo, Griso, some Bravi who stop at the bottom of the scene exploring.
Perpetua, peasants, ind Agnese.
Renzo, Lucia, Tonio, Gervaso leaving the house of Don Abbondio; then peasants armed with scythes and hoes. Don Abbondio to the window. Agnes and Perpetua.

The shore of the Adda on the place called the Bione near Pescarenico. You can see, near, the triangular bell tower of the convent. Beyond the Adda promontori and mountains. - It is night. Lucia, Agnese, a Barcaiolo.
Renzo, the father Christopher, and said.

In a village at the foot of the mountain; in front of the right, the parish house with a large door that puts to a courtyard. Balcony covered with rich carpets. Large avenue leading to the church. Archies of triumph, curtains, sandals, decorations of all kinds. Behind the village, a promontory, not far away, where a castle rises. (*) Men and Women coming from different streets; others coming out of the courtyard of the parish house.
The unnamed and said.
Don Abbondio, Perpetua, turn to the Choir.
Agnese entering fatigued by the race, in Perpetua.

Don Abbondio who advances on horseback, surrounded by the Folla. Lucia who comes out of the litter and takes himself to the front of the scene embraced Agnes. The unnamed, Perpetua, Bravi, Popolo; finally Cardinal Federico Borromeo with followers of Prelates.
Anticamera in the palace of Don Rodrigo, in Milan. Middle door, other door to the right, few chairs, a counter. Griso lying on a counter, in the end don Rodrigo. (*)

The vast esplanade of the lazzaretto of Milan. On the right and at the bottom the porch. At the left side, at the end of the scene, a cross. (*) Renzo. The song of the monasteries resounds in the distance, and therefore completely ceases.
Renzo. Procession of women coming out of the porch to the left and moving towards the cross. Lucia last.
Between Christopher and sayings.
